summary: Added a deterministic, stdlib-only NLI/semantic-conflict production-readiness scaffold that distinguishes the existing deterministic LEXICAL conflict detector (is_real_nli_model=false, does_semantic_entailment=false) from a real NLI/LLM setup. map_nli_label_to_verdict deterministically maps SNLI/MNLI (entailment/contradiction/neutral) and FEVER/CFEVER (supports/refutes/NEI) labels to canonical verdicts supports/refutes/not_enough_info, raising on unknown labels. build_nli_provider_readiness / validate_nli_provider_config classify a provider config, requiring a real provider + model + credential_source (env var NAME, never a value) and rejecting credential-shaped fields. build_semantic_conflict_policy / validate_semantic_conflict_policy describe and check a decision policy (verdict labels, min_confidence in [0,1], block_on/warn_on). build_semantic_conflict_readiness aggregates into a production_ready verdict true only for a complete DECLARED config with eval labels covering all three verdicts, and always reports current_shipped_state.production_ready=false. A CLI tools/check_semantic_conflict_readiness.py exits nonzero on the repo default. No model call, no download, no network, no credential/.env read; the existing lexical detector is unchanged and the original ROADMAP item stays unchecked with a checked sub-note.

risks: production_ready=true is a CONFIG-COMPLETENESS verdict, not a connectivity/authentication/evaluation check; a fully-declared but wrong config would read as ready. It gates human intent, it does not run NLI or an eval.
map_nli_label_to_verdict collapses 'neutral' and 'NEI' to not_enough_info; a downstream policy that needs to distinguish genuine neutrality from missing evidence would need a richer mapping.
The scaffold reads only declared metadata and never resolves credential_source to a secret, so it cannot confirm a credential is present or valid.

The existing lexical detect_conflict_evidence is deliberately untouched; enabling real NLI later must register a provider and only then read config/credentials, and would need its own eval before replacing lexical output.

Environment note: the local interpreter is python3 (no bare 'python' on PATH); the quality-gate runner honors PYTHON=python3, and a local 'python->python3' PATH shim lets its default-interpreter meta-test pass.
credentials: No credentials or .env files were read, created, or modified; NLI validators reject credential-shaped value fields and the scaffold uses only a credential_source env-var NAME.
No external network calls, model calls, or model downloads were used for implementation or local tests.
